trick: The two Latin roots pull in opposite directions and both are right: 'educare' means to bring up or nourish from outside, 'educere' means to draw out what is already within. Narrow education is what school does; wider education is everything life does, from birth to death.

video.query: meaning and concept of education narrow and wider sense class 11

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about the concept of education.

items.statement: Education in the wider sense ends when schooling ends.
items.why: The wider sense is lifelong — a person learns from family, work and society long after leaving school.

items.statement: 'Educere' means to draw out the powers already latent in the child.
items.why: It is the root behind the view that the teacher unfolds what is within, rather than pouring in from outside.

items.statement: Education is a bipolar process according to Adams.
items.why: Adams described two poles, the teacher and the taught. John Dewey later called it tripolar by adding the social environment.

items.statement: In the narrow sense, education means the planned instruction given in a school.
items.why: Narrow education is deliberate, institutional and limited in time — the classroom sense of the word.

items.statement: Education and instruction mean the same thing.
items.why: Instruction is the passing on of information; education is the whole development of the person, including character and attitude.

chapter: Agencies of Education: Family, School and Informal
trick: An agency is formal if it teaches deliberately with a syllabus, informal if it teaches without meaning to. The family is the child's first and most informal school; the radio and the cinema teach a great deal while intending only to entertain.

chapter: Philosophical Foundations: Idealism, Buddhism and Jainism
trick: Idealism puts the idea and the spirit first, so its aim is self-realisation and its method is the teacher's example. Buddhism aims at the end of suffering through the Eightfold Path; Jainism aims at liberation through the three jewels and ahimsa. Each philosophy's aim of education is simply its idea of the good life, restated for the child.

Learning through the teacher's personal example and great books

trick: IQ is mental age divided by chronological age, times 100 — the mental age is always on top. So a bright child of 8 who performs like a 10-year-old scores 10/8 × 100 = 125. If you ever write it the other way up, every dull child comes out brilliant, which is the quickest way to catch the mistake.

video.query: intelligence quotient formula mental age spearman two factor theory class 11

data.prompt: Work out an IQ, then check you have the formula the right way up.
data.problem: Riya is 8 years old. On a standard test she performs as well as an average 10-year-old.

steps.why: Mental age is the age group whose average performance she matches — here, 10.
Mental age goes on top. Written the other way round, a child who is behind would score above 100.

steps.ask: A child of 10 with a mental age of 8 scores what?
steps.why: (8 ÷ 10) × 100 = 80 — below average, which is the sense check that the formula is the right way up.

data.answer: IQ = (Mental age ÷ Chronological age) × 100. Riya scores 125; the second child scores 80.

trick: Sort the schemes by who they are for: SSA is elementary schooling for all, RMSA is the secondary stage, Mid-Day Meal is nutrition and attendance together, and the RTE Act 2009 is the law that gives the whole thing teeth. Dates matter here — SSA 2001, RTE Act 2009, in force from 1 April 2010.
